subject: Question about R code: stoping and restarting a for loop if condition does not meet

messages.author: 07173b85d9b339bd
messages.subject: Question about R code: stoping and restarting a for loop if condition does not meet
parts:
Hi all

I have a question about a script I wrote for assessing a experimental design for in terms of a D-optimality criterion.

Below is the whole code.  It worked well with simpler designs I tried before. However, this last week I tried to find a efficient design for other larger case and I got some errors.  Basically, the error I got has to do with some designs for which the code can not get the inverse of matrix A (solve(A)) , one of the steps of calculating the D-error.  Even though I put the condition that det(A) not to be equal to 0, the program now stops for some designs, not all of them.

Therefore, what I would like to do is to make the program to restart the loop everytime it can not solve A, so it gets a new design, evaluates D.error and counts each time it can not calculate D.error.  I have tried things like: breakFlag or break and it is not working, the system stops but do not return to start the evaluation of a new design.

Sorry, the code might be very simple and  what I need to do too, I am new in writing codes in R.

Thanks in advance for any help,
Susana


## Code starts here##

set.seed(26)
nreps=200
repsmat <- list()
derror <-list()
for (r in 1:nreps){
data=read.table(file="descod2s1000p.txt",header=FALSE,sep=" ")
nvers=40
data<-as.matrix(data)
j <- sample (1:1000,nvers, replace=FALSE)
repsmat[[r]] <- j
candes <- matrix (data=0, nrow=nvers,ncol=198)
  for (k in 1:12){
    candes[k,1:198]<-data[j[k],1:198 ]
}
Palt=(1/3)
mat <- NULL
for (i in 1:nvers){
  m <- matrix(candes[i, ], ncol=22, byrow=TRUE)
  mat <- rbind(mat, m)
}
zmat <- matrix(data=0,nrow=108,ncol=22)
for (i in 1:108){
  for(j in 1:22){
    zmat[i,j]<-mat[i,j]-sum(mat[i, ])*Palt
  }
}
#Calculating D.error
P<-as.matrix((1/3)*diag(108))
Zt<-t(zmat)
Ztzmat<-(Zt%*%zmat)
A=Zt%*%P%*%zmat
if(det(Ztzmat)<=0.99){
  derror[[r]] <- NA  
} else {
sigma=(solve(A))
D.error=(det(sigma))^(1/nvers)
derror[[r]] <- D.error}
}
sureval<-do.call(rbind, repsmat)
derror2<-do.call(rbind, derror)
result.derror<-cbind(derror2,sureval)
ressorted<-result.derror[sort.list(result.derror[,1]), ]
write.table(ressorted, file='resultderrors2s3.txt', row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE)

### end of code

This is the error I got

## error 
 D.error=(det(sigma))^(1/nvers)
+ derror[[r]] <- D.error}
+ }
Error in solve.default(A) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 2.32347e-18
> sureval<-do.call(rbind, repsmat)
> derror2<-do.call(rbind, derror)
> result.derror<-cbind(derror2,sureval)
>Error in cbind(derror2, sureval) : 
  number of rows of matrices must match (see arg 2)




--
*********************************************
Susana Cardenas
Graduate Group in Ecology
University of California, Davis

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Question about R code: stoping and restarting a for loop if condition does not meet
parts:
Susana,

You can use try() to catch the error and use it to determine the next step in your code. The expression

x <- try(expr, silent = FALSE)

will assign x the value of the expression unless there is an error, which case x will be the error message.

I can't test this without your data file, but I think what you want to do is this:

sigma=try(solve(A), silent=TRUE)
if(class(sigma)="try-error") {
  derror[[r]] <- NA
} else {
  D.error=(det(sigma))^(1/nvers)
  derror[[r]] <- D.error}
}

You may want to save the error messages, as well, if you want to diagnose why the matrices are unsolvable.
